description: Timeline comparison of Bitcoin (BTC) network value and two major competitor chains—Bitcoin Cash (BCH) and Bitcoin SV (BSV)—through the 2017 split, the 2018-2021 crypto bear/boom cycles, and the 2024-2025 stabilization. Built for a dramatic chart-race style visualization.
youtube_description:
🧨 Bitcoin wasn’t just “one chain”—it was a battlefield. In 2017, a governance dispute detonated the ecosystem, spawning Bitcoin Cash (BCH) and Bitcoin SV (BSV). This timeline comparison tracks the market value race across the same macro cycles: the 2017 breakout, the 2018 crash, the 2020-2021 bull run, and the 2022-2024 reset.

Chapters
00:00 — The fork that split belief (2017)
01:05 — 2018’s purge: who survived the crash
02:10 — 2020’s rebound: attention shifts back to BTC
03:15 — 2021 bull spike: BCH briefly catches heat
04:30 — 2022 bear: BCH and BSV lose gravity
05:35 — 2023-2024 stabilization: BTC solidifies dominance
06:40 — 2025-2026: where the fork era ends up

What you’re seeing in the chart-race:
• BTC’s dominance reasserts after each wave of hype.
• BCH experiences “second-life” rallies, but it never recaptures its early fork-era share.
• BSV becomes a persistent niche—never dead, but structurally capped.

📌 Call to action
If you want more chart-race datasets like this (real-world market-cap timelines with dramatic crossover moments), hit like, subscribe, and comment which fork you think should have won.

instagram_caption:
🚀 The Bitcoin fork didn’t just change code—it reshaped power.

In 2017, the “Bitcoin future” became a fight you could measure in money. When the chain-split erupted, Bitcoin (BTC) entered the year at about **$260B** in market value. But the fork created two rivals—**Bitcoin Cash (BCH)** at roughly **$12B**, and **Bitcoin SV (BSV)** barely above launch-range at about **$0.6B**. This is where the timeline gets violent: the same headline, three different fates.

Then comes 2018—the purge year. BTC crashes hard from the breakout era, falling to about **$130B**. BCH gets hit even harder, sliding to around **$5B**. And BSV drops into micro-cap territory (about **$0.2B**). The message is clear: forks can rally, but survival depends on the market’s willingness to keep paying for legitimacy.

By 2020, BTC rebounds into the spotlight at roughly **$380B**. BCH tries to reignite—around **$6B**—while BSV climbs modestly to about **$1.5B**. But 2021 is the real drama: BTC rockets to about **$920B**, while BCH spikes to nearly **$18B** (for a moment, it looks like the fork could matter again). BSV rises too—near **$5B**—yet the gap remains enormous.

The 2022 bear market reorders the chessboard. BTC falls to about **$280B**, BCH sinks to **$6B**, and BSV to about **$1.2B**. From there, the story tightens: in 2023 and 2024, BTC stabilizes at **$720B → $1.02T**, while BCH drifts—**$8B → $4B**—and BSV stays niche at roughly **$0.7B → $1.0B**.

By 2025-2026, the fork era looks like a permanent echo—not a takeover. BTC sits around **$1.08T → $1.12T**, while BCH hovers near **$6B → $7B** and BSV around **$1.3B → $1.6B**.

Be honest: if you could pick one—**BTC, BCH, or BSV**—which fork do you think deserved to win long-term dominance? Comment your pick, and I’ll make a follow-up chart-race.
facebook_caption:
The Bitcoin fork era wasn’t a footnote—it was a measurable market power shift. Starting in 2017, BTC sat at about $260B market capitalization, while BCH launched the split at roughly $12B and BSV at about $0.6B. The 2018 crash sharply separated winners from survivors: BTC fell to around $130B, BCH to about $5B, and BSV to near $0.2B.

Across the 2020-2021 bull cycle, BTC surged to approximately $920B by 2021. BCH briefly re-accelerated to around $18B, while BSV rose to roughly $5B. But the 2022 bear market reset the momentum: BTC dropped to around $280B; BCH fell back to about $6B; and BSV declined to near $1.2B. In 2023-2024, BTC strengthened to roughly $720B then $1.02T, while BCH drifted to around $8B then $4B, and BSV remained a niche chain near $0.7B to $1.0B.

By 2025-2026, BTC concentrates value near $1.08T–$1.12T, while BCH and BSV stabilize far below that level—turning the fork frenzy into long-term dominance-by-BTC.

threads_caption:
Forks are chaos—until the charts settle it. 👀

2017: BTC at ~$260B, BCH at ~$12B, BSV at ~$0.6B.
2018: BTC dips to ~$130B, BCH to ~$5B, BSV to ~$0.2B.
2021: BTC explodes to ~$920B… BCH pops to ~$18B… BSV hits ~$5B.
Then 2022 resets everything: BTC ~$280B, BCH ~$6B, BSV ~$1.2B.

By 2025-2026, BTC is basically in its own league (~$1.08T–$1.12T), while BCH (~$6B–$7B) and BSV (~$1.3B–$1.6B) stay niche.

Real talk: was the fork “innovation,” “fragmentation,” or just temporary hype?
